previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and prior left index finger amputation due to steal syndrome was admitted for a dehisced wound with signs of infection, including swelling, pain, and prior pus. Cultures from clinic identified E. coli, and the patient had been started on Augmentin. He was admitted for IV antibiotics, pain control, and wound care. Imaging showed no osteomyelitis. Treatment included IV Zosyn, transition to oral Bactrim and ciprofloxacin, daily Betadine soaks, and hand elevation. His diabetes was poorly controlled with glucose levels in the 200–300 mg/dL range, prompting consultation with Endocrinology and initiation of glargine insulin with a sliding scale. The patient remained afebrile, stable, and pain-controlled throughout the stay. He was discharged home on a 7-day course of oral antibiotics, continued insulin regimen, and instructions for wound care and follow-up with Hand Clinic and Endocrinology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ gentleman with h/o ESRD now s/p renal transplant x2 and 
IDDM who presents with chronic nonhealing left finger wound and 
fevers.

# Left index finger gangrene - Pt. admitted with nonhealing left 
index finger wound and fevers.  Nonhealing wound due to steal 
syndrome from old fistula.  Already with history of 
osteomyelitis in that finger and left DIP joint amputation. 
Since that amputation earlier this year, the finger failed to 
heal and over the days prior to admission, he developed 
increasing erythema and edema with significant purulent 
drainage.  He was started on antibiotics ___ and promptly 
underwent ray amputation of left index finger on ___.  
Cultures from wound swab and biopsy both grew e. coli 
susceptible to ertapenem.  Post-operatively, the patient did 
well on antibiotics.  He had severe inciscional and neuropathic 
pain initially, but this soon resolved. A PICC line was placed 
in order for the pt. to complete a 6 week course of IV ertapenem 
as an outpatient.   He will follow-up with hand surgery as well 
as infectiuos disease.  

# Bacteremia - Blood cultures on admission grew E. coli 
susceptible to ertapenem.  Infected finger was likely source.  
Subsquent surveillance cultures were all negative. He was 
treated with meropenem while in patient and then switched to 
ertapenem on discharge (as above).   

# Acute on chronic renal failure - Pt. with history of renal 
transplant x 2 in ___ with baseline creatinine around 1.1-1.3.  
On admission, his Cr was initially elevated at 1.7. It initially 
decreased with fluid administration, but then rose again 
post-operatively.  He had been placed on gabapentin briefly for 
pain and this was discontinued.  He was also given further 
hydration and PO intake encouraged.  By discharge, his 
creatinine had returned to baseline at 1.2.  

# Hypertension - Pt. w/ history of labile BPs in the past, 
though recently had been well controlled per pt. report.  
Unfortunately, during this admission, his blood pressure 
repeatedly rose into the SBP 180s, though the pt. remained 
asymptomatic.  His home antihypertensives were continued, and 
this was initially felt to be related to pain.  His blood 
pressure on discharge was mildly elevated, and he had close 
follow-up with his primary care physician for BP check. 

# DM - Home insulin initially reduced given poor PO, but rapidly 
uptitrated to home dose of glargine 26U in the evening. 

# S/p renal transplant x 2 (___) - Pt. was continued on home 
tacrolimus and prednisone.  His tacro levels indicated 
therapetic dosing.  He was continued on prophylactic bactrim.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Index finger partial amputation with pain and skin necrosis,
concerning for osteomyelitis.  Of note, the requisition indicates that it is
the right index finger, though the patient states it is the left.

COMPARISONS:  Left index finger radiographs from ___.  MRI of
the hand from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  PA, lateral, and oblique views of the left hand were obtained with
a total of three exposures.  PA and oblique views of the left index finger
were obtained with a total of two exposures.

FINDINGS:  Since the prior exam, there is increased heterogeneity of the bone
around the second PIP with some evidence of cortical irregularity and loss of
joint space.  This is concerning for osteomyelitis.  This irregularity extends
more proximally with possible cortical destruction of the medial aspect of the
second proximal phalanx.  There is new subcutaneous gas around the joint. 
There is no evidence of radiopaque foreign body.  Atherosclerotic
calcifications are noted.

No fracture or osseous destruction is noted elsewhere in the hand. 
Atherosclerotic calcifications are severe.

IMPRESSION:  Increased osseous destruction and subcutaneous air around the
second PIP is concerning for osteomyelitis and soft tissue infection.

Results were discussed directly with the on-call plastic surgery resident at
7:15 p.m. on ___ in person by Dr. ___ at the time the findings were
discovered.

AP CHEST, 8:26 A.M. ON ___

HISTORY:  Decreased breath sounds.  Preop.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Lungs are hyperinflated, an indication of small airway obstruction or perhaps
emphysema, but clear of any focal abnormality.  There is no pleural effusion
or evidence of central lymph node enlargement.  Heart size is top normal.

HISTORY:  Renal transplant x2 now presenting with elevated creatinine.  

TECHNIQUE:  Real-time grayscale and duplex Doppler ultrasound of the renal
transplant 

COMPARISON:  ___.  

FINDINGS:

TRANSPLANT KIDNEY: 

Echogenicity:  Normal.  
Focal lesions:  None.  
Hydronephrosis:  None.  
Peritransplant fluid:  None.  

INTRARENAL ARTERIES:

Waveforms:  Unchanged from the prior studies with relatively brisk systolic
upstroke.  
Resistive indicies (Upper, Mid, Lower Pole):  0.73, 0.72, 0.73 respectively.  

MAIN RENAL ARTERY AND VEIN:  

Both are patent with a 0.75 resistive index in the main renal artery and
appropriate brisk systolic upstroke.  

BLADDER:  Partially distended and unremarkable 

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of obstruction.  Patent transplant arterial vasculature with near
normal renal indices ranging from 0.72-0.75.

HISTORY:  New right PICC line.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal radiograph of the chest shows a new right PICC with tip of
the catheter in the low portion of the SVC.  No pneumothorax is seen. 
Otherwise, the lungs are clear and the cardiomediastinal contours are normal.

IMPRESSION:  Satisfactory position of right PICC with the tip in the low SVC.
